title: This Shrimp Kills With a Bubble Hotter Than 4,000 Degrees
subject: pistol shrimp

scenes.text: This shrimp never touches its prey. A bubble does the killing.
The pistol shrimp has one oversized claw, about half the size of its body.
It snaps the claw shut, and a jet of water shoots out at about 60 miles an hour.
The jet drops pressure so low that a bubble forms, then collapses in a fraction of a second.
The collapse hits over 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit and a pop of 218 decibels, louder than a gunshot.
It even flashes light. A shrimp, a bubble, and a pop that stuns whatever it aimed at.

description:
A pistol shrimp snaps its claw and shoots a jet of water at about 60 miles an hour.
The jet creates a bubble that collapses with a 218 decibel pop and temperatures above 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit, and a flash of light.
What other animal uses physics as a weapon? Comment below.
first_comment: Which is scarier: a pistol shrimp or a mantis shrimp? Both are smaller than your hand.
